# Deliver explicit EQ and input-filter previews through browser and headless SDKs

Astra xhigh rescope, 2026-09-13. Authority: the original parent text through “Related work and handoff boundary,” before our appended implementation staging. Source: merged main `1cb18a26c3c12a12a4afd133633ab9cd5a44600e`; paused #774 checkpoint `4083eb68` inspected for reusable work. Earlier unnumbered briefs are superseded by this plan. Preserve merged working code and the paused branch/history. No implementation, builds or GitHub edits were performed in this rescope.

## Requirements and acceptance — before implementation choices

The parent is complete only when all of these work:

- **Engine-owned discovery and selection:** generated capabilities from effect and graph/tap owners; explicit targets, channels, fields, resolution/cadence; supported/unavailable distinguishable from silence. Discover/query/subscribe-update/read/close; normalized effective configuration/resources; atomic admission and typed refusal. Runtime stable IDs bind to actual plan-scoped handles. Identical jobs share only identical semantics; bounded reference counts; last close stops work; replacement invalidates old handles/results.
- **Response:** production EQ total/optional four bands and builtin HPF/LPF, independent L/R, enables/bypass, engine-provided grids, finite declared floors and owner-correct rounded-word recurrence. Declared linear EQ/filter composition reports actual order/membership and honest subtotal exclusions. Explicit previews carry `requestedConfiguration` and a configuration identity; applied-target/live responses require actual render-owned immutable snapshots, state identity and effective/captured sample, change-driven recomputation and coalescing. Queued/requested never means audible.
- **Spectrum:** actual engine post-input-builtins, post-matrix and final-output taps; declared real FFT/Hann/bin/hop/normalization/floor; independent L/R; power smoothing with explicit time/history and unsmoothed option. Warm-up, gap/seek/nonfinite resets and known rendered-underrun validity. No source-ring substitute, client FFT, invented resolution or audio mutation/latency.
- **Common time and results:** existing u64 render clock; distinguish clock instance, actual session/plan, content discontinuity, state, publication sequence/epoch and loss. Honest discriminated spans/state times; per-effect GR retains its original span/sequence and legacy aggregates remain available with honest join limitations. JS bigint/binary u64/JSON decimal strings, including >2^53. Bounded sample join reports complete/partial/stale/missing/gap and age, including parameter changes inside FFT windows; processing/PDC latency separate from capture time.
- **Portable execution and bounded transport:** same Rust analysis for native worker, deterministic headless pump and dedicated browser Worker. Render performs only bounded prepared copies/snapshot publication: no FFT/log, allocation/free, locks, waits/wakes/syscalls or analysis in Worklet message handlers. Bounded ownership slots, no overwrite of reader-owned data, saturation counters/reset. Browser SAB and bounded pooled-transfer fallback, qualified under existing realtime gates; unsupported fallback must be explicit until qualified. Bounded messages/backlogs as well as buffers, no UI FFT.
- **Efficient interfaces and compatibility:** owned stable SDK arrays; efficient native read-into; packed additive capability-gated remote vectors, axes/maps once per configuration, alignment/endianness validation, no PCM control transport or per-bin MeterRecord expansion. Preserve existing scalar/meter/ABI contracts. Configurable jobs/channels/points/FFT/rate/memory/pool budgets, no compiled track ceiling or duration growth; no capture/compute/traffic while unsubscribed.
- **Evidence and adoption:** representative independent curve/PCM and FFT correctness, four launch rates, native/Wasm parity, bank/tail/asymmetric lanes, bit-identical audio, u64/time/lifecycle/slow-worker/saturation/churn/seek/replace cases, resource and existing realtime gates. Actual SDK browser/headless examples and browser execution; docs replace client source-spectrum advice while preserving the low-level observer. One frozen descriptive transport/resource comparison after the feature works. Engine/SDK delivery and synchronized evidence close the parent; app edits/deployment are outside this repository outcome.

**Explicitly allowed later:** the original first-query checkpoint permits input filters/composition in a bounded successor before parent closure; this rescope includes input filters immediately and composition next. Frozen instantaneous-word mode, arbitrary per-effect taps, phase/group delay, nonlinear transfer estimates, device-clock synchronization, extended compatibility matrices and optimization frameworks are outside the first scope/as expressly allowed by the parent. Live target, required taps/spectrum, lifecycle, SDK parity, packed remote vectors and joins remain required inside #763. FFT 2048, periodic Hann, amplitude dBFS and 30 Hz are sensible proposed profile choices, not immutable user-chosen algorithms; freeze the actual profile before that implementation.

**Choices we added, not original requirements:** a prepared-session catalog before any SDK query; a full-session request-projection refactor for explicit preview; two new boot/SDK identity systems before live binding; a persistent preview handle registry; individual-allocation accounting taxonomy; particular raw-magnitude trait/accumulator types; three more native/host precursor issues; repeated artifact issues and extensive test-name/ABI prose before a usable endpoint. Drop these as prerequisites. Bounded resources, correct numerical composition and actual live identity remain requirements, but those particular mechanisms do not.

## Next issue: explicit EQ/input-filter preview through both SDKs

**Approve for immediate Luna max implementation on a fresh branch from main.** Create a new numbered issue with this scope; do not rewrite #774's failed/pending acceptance history. Keep #774 at `4083eb68` for later reuse. Carry only its small validated frequency-grid helper/tests into the new implementation, not its catalog/provider/target/generation machinery. No further native-only delivery boundary precedes the SDK.

**User outcome:** browser and Node/Bun callers use the shipped SDK to discover and request a named explicit EQ configuration or input HPF/LPF configuration, while stopped, and receive engine-computed totals/optional sections, engine frequencies and independent owned channel arrays. An app can remove its EQ/filter transfer calculation. This is an explicit configuration utility; it neither reads nor claims to describe an active session. No boot identity, full-session compile, graph lookup or audio engine is needed.

Minimal public shape (equivalent concise naming permitted):

```ts
const preview = await createResponsePreview({ asset, limits });
preview.capabilities; // Generated engine owner declarations.
const result = await preview.query({
  configurationId: 7n,
  sampleRateHz: 48000,
  quantumFrames: 128,
  configuration: effect("<generated EQ id>", { /* existing named parameters */ }),
  targetCorrelation: { trackId: "vocal", rack: "simd1", slotId: "tone" },
  grid: { kind: "logarithmic", points: 256, minimumHz: 20, maximumHz: 20000 },
  channels: "both", fields: "totalAndSections",
});
await preview.close();
```

The other configuration variant is `{ kind: "inputFilters", left: { hpfHz, lpfHz }, right: { hpfHz, lpfHz } }`. Reuse SDK `effect()`/generated parameter names, enums and per-lane values; no new EQ-specific parameter syntax or table. One owner per query is enough for this first slice. `targetCorrelation` is caller metadata for the explicitly supplied configuration, **not a resolved plan binding**. Return it honestly as correlation. No target/effective sample, plan epoch or active-state identity. The later live slice owns actual stable-ID binding/invalidation. No implicit all-track or live subscription.

The result supplies `requestedConfiguration`, unchanged bigint configuration ID, sample rate, normalized grid/configuration (including effective defaults/enables/bypass), declared floor/units/section order, `frequenciesHz: Float32Array`, and only the requested channel total/section arrays. Empty/unavailable capability and malformed/unsupported requests are typed refusals. Expose constructor limits and actual request/result/owner retained bytes; no pretend zero-copy or live-state claim.

### Implementation: reuse first, add a thin bridge

1. **Rust preparation/query:** add one small host-core response-query module (including its native caller-buffer API), not a session catalog. Resolve effect native IDs through `effect_compiler::launch_native_effect_registry()` and `factory.response_analysis()`. `effect_contract::default_initial_values(descriptor)` already emits the exact descriptor-order/channel defaults; apply explicit numeric parameter-ID/channel/value overrides to that list, reject unknown/duplicate/conflicting channels, then let the existing `prepare_response`/`expected_prepared_metadata` validate it. This is direct explicit configuration, not a second Session compiler. Reuse generated SDK normalization for names/enums; Rust remains the domain/default authority. Pass the requested rate/quantum/quality/link/bypass and declared no-sidechain configuration; unsupported owners/options refuse. Never call `factory.prepare`, full session preparation or render.
2. **Input filters and grids:** use existing `builtins::BuiltinParameters::default()` with explicit L/R HPF/LPF values and `prepare_input_filter_response`. Other builtins remain excluded by its existing descriptor. Reuse only #774's small grid validator/generator: portable `math::{log,exp}`, f64 interpolation with f64 subtraction, exact f32 endpoints, strict finite/increasing/in-range validation at four launch rates. Do not touch accepted owner response math. Existing `PreparedResponseAnalysis::query_into` supplies curves. The current owner API computes both lanes; budget a temporary unwanted lane when only one is requested, rather than refactor owners to optimize it now.
3. **Wasm boundary:** `hosts/host-web/src/{lib,ffi}.rs` gets a small analysis-only request/result adapter calling that helper. Reuse pointer/length/staging conventions; add only necessary V1 exports and a Rust-defined fixed request/header plus numeric override records. Generate offsets/constants from Rust through the existing ABI tool. The record carries owner native ID, explicit preparation fields, bigint configuration ID, grid/fields/channels and byte/point limits; contiguous f32 result buffers carry axis/totals/sections. One request workspace, one active call, one owned result; no handle registry, generic protocol, whole-session JSON, dynamic target catalog, new serde dependency, or compatibility-layer rewrite. Checked counts/ranges/caps and typed status precede allocation/output publication. The adapter works in a Wasm instance whose audio host was never booted.
4. **Discovery and SDK:** `tools/parameter-metadata/src/lib.rs` emits the existing factory/builtin response descriptor under the existing generated catalog. Query each registry factory, never maintain a host/JS EQ-ID table; unavailable native owners remain explicit. Update `abi_layout.rs`, existing strict metadata/export validators, `sdk/codegen`, generated assets/types normally. Add shared `sdk/src/core/response.ts` for the small query API/encoding and thin browser/headless factories. `sdk/src/core/session.ts::parameterRows` already translates display names/enums to numeric ID/channel/value rows; share that helper internally if needed instead of duplicating it. Unknown modes/fields refuse. No spectrum/live capabilities are advertised yet.
5. **Browser execution:** add `sdk/src/browser/response-worker.ts` and a small controller using the current scratch Worker's ready/request/error/timeout/termination pattern. Instantiate the compiled `MisoEngineAsset.module` in that Worker and call only analysis exports, never `WasmBoundary.boot` or the scratch rehearsal body. Headless instantiates the same asset directly without boot and calls the same adapter. Export through existing browser/headless barrels; add the Worker URL to `sdk/src/assets.ts`. No Worklet host/process/message changes are needed for an explicit utility. One outstanding request per preview instance; concurrent query gets backpressure; close is idempotent and terminates/rejects pending work. Copy Wasm outputs to exact owned ArrayBuffers and transfer Worker results once. Recreate memory views after growing calls. No job cache, automatic reopen, persistent thread pool or performance tuning.

**Boundary:** production changes stay in the thin host-core/host-web adapter, existing metadata/ABI generators and validators, shared/browser/headless SDK entry points, worker asset packaging and docs. Existing dependency `host-core -> math` may be added for the reused grid helper; host-web already depends on host-core and need not gain effect-compiler. Preserve legacy ABI layouts/symbol semantics; additive exports/metadata are legitimate changes. No effect-compiler projection refactor, graph/render changes, active plan identity, #774 catalog import, new package/harness or optimization. Small local request/layout choices are Luna's implementation work within this frozen contract; do not require another design round.

## Complete the remaining parent through working extensions

Keep the requirements checklist above as the completion ledger. Do not build separate generic infrastructure before its first consumer. The following order preserves the full scope while putting every product path through the SDK:

1. **SDK composition:** extend the working query to an explicitly supplied ordered EQ/filter chain; owners provide an unfloored f64 magnitude primitive only as needed, combine before floor, report ordered membership and exclusions, always label the subtotal honestly. Reuse existing query transport/Worker. Integrate typed session order (`input`, SIMD1, dynamic, SIMD2) and actual stable binding when the live slice attaches to the real graph; never claim caller-specified order is current graph order. Composition over the actual current graph remains required, not replaced by the explicit-chain utility. Tests target floor recovery/zero/nonfinite, L/R/bypass and order, not a new numerical framework. If adding explicit-chain composition would duplicate the later actual-graph path, fold composition into step 2 instead; no standalone raw-primitive issue.
2. **Live responses + existing per-effect observations:** extend `effect-compiler::EffectObservationHandle`/readers, `host-core::PreparedHost.effect_observations`, `engine::realtime::observe`, rack control drains and `plan_exchange` with the minimum real stable binding, bounded admission/shared jobs and lifecycle needed by live EQ/GR. Publish small owner snapshots at real sample boundaries; evaluate through the working Worker/pump and return actual u64 envelopes, unchanged suppression and close/invalidation. Expose original GR windows, preserve aggregates. Incorporate composed current-graph EQ/filter responses here if not already done. Introduce one actual engine/plan generation where owned, not parallel fake identity schemes. A request/snapshot is not an audio-engine clone. Deliver native, headless and browser together; if too large, split live EQ and existing GR delivery into separately usable SDK changes, not foundation-only layers.
3. **Spectrum end to end:** use `graph-compiler/src/ids.rs`'s existing `SendTap`/`TrackStage` mapping and actual graph/rack execution boundaries for the three required taps. Add only prepared selected capture storage/ownership; do not repurpose scalar cells. Reuse `engine::realtime::spsc`/ownership patterns, prove no reader overwrite and no render wake. The repo has a direct DFT oracle in `dsp-reference/src/spectrum.rs` but no production FFT found: choose one small portable real-FFT implementation/dependency at this step, freeze the profile, then wire it through the existing preview Worker and headless pump. Deliver required tap selection, spectra and status in the SDK before extended evidence. Start with SAB capture; then qualify bounded pooled-transfer fallback as its own usable non-isolated-browser extension if necessary, advertising unavailable until it works. Native/headless capture/FFT and browser capture are legitimate usable boundaries if one slice exceeds half a day; no capture-only completion claim.
4. **Finish common integration:** add vector messages through existing `protocol::{message_wire,btlv}` and its caller-buffer tests; use compact f32 vectors, not scalar bins. Add bounded join over the actual delivered response/GR/spectrum envelopes, effective state events and existing peaks, preserving unknown aggregate timing. Finish examples/docs, resource reports and every remaining checklist item, then run the single frozen descriptive comparison with existing harnesses. Slow-consumer/churn/seek/parameter-inside-window/plan-replacement tests belong to the feature that first implements each behavior, not an up-front general certification framework. No optimization until the full functional path works and evidence identifies a concrete bottleneck.

This is a progression, not four oversized implementation authorizations: number each next usable change only when the preceding path works, carrying the outstanding checklist unchanged. The **immediately executable authorization is the explicit browser/headless EQ + input-filter preview above**. #774 and previous briefs provide optional reusable code, not architecture requirements or a reason to delay the SDK again.
